label: miso22 offer curve
definition: One architectural lever on top of miso21 (all prior levers retained: export cap, cc_intermediate_split, miso_pjm_border_anchor, firm-import/seam-flow/coal-mustrun/sigmoid stack): MISO receives its own ISO-specific gas offer curve (_MISO_OFFER_CURVE, deep-merged on iso=="MISO"), the same design PJM, NYISO, and CAISO already use, replacing the inherited ERCOT-fit generic fallback that had never been validated for MISO. Two gas classes change, all others keep the generic default. CC_REGULAR econ ramp flattened econ_low 1.06->0.95 / econ_high 1.27->1.08 to match MISO's measured all-baseload CC shape (CAMPD: 44 CC_REGULAR plants, cap-weighted HR 7.44, median CF 50-150%); committed base (0.92) and duct-burner scarcity peak (2.25) are physically unchanged. CT_PEAKER peak capped 13.15->4.0 to MISO's offer-cap-consistent level, removing the inherited ERCOT ORDC $5000 wall (same reasoning PJM used), with committed and econ ramp left at the generic shape. Metric-neutral vs miso21 (cc_intermediate_split already routed MISO's baseload CC cohort to the flat curve; 0 scarcity hours so the CT cap has zero dispatch effect): every fuel class within +-0.6 TWh of miso21, 2025 system volume marginally better. Value is architectural consolidation + correct CC base + removed ERCOT wall, not residual closure. NOT-YET: residual CC_REGULAR over-run / CT+ST under-run (import under-run root cause), 2025 dear-gas coal over-run (+13.8 TWh), import under-run 2024/25, and 0 scarcity hours are open MODEL MISS items; exceptions ledger empty.
